correctness.rationale: In a local nonfield with square-zero maximal ideal, unit orbits in the nonzero radical are exactly projective directions over the residue field. The source entry formula then gives identical columns for all such directions, so rank is at most three. The unit column, one projective-direction column and the zero column have determinant minus h times q squared after compression and are independent, so local rank is exactly three. A field factor has the displayed two-by-two full-rank matrix. The source direct-product identity makes the global matrix a Kronecker product, so ranks multiply. A fresh symbolic calculation reproduced the determinant and the packaged exact verifier independently checks fifteen local parameter cells and four tensor products.

value.rationale: The theorem answers the source paper's explicit rank question on the first broad non-Frobenius layer where singularity alone gives no rank information. The independence from radical embedding dimension is a structural phenomenon and the factorwise formula is reusable for arbitrary products of square-zero local rings.

final_claim: For a finite commutative ring with square-zero Jacobson radical, each field local factor contributes local Ramanujan-matrix rank two and each nonfield local factor contributes rank three; hence the global rank is the product of those local contributions.
limitations: The Jacobson radical must square to zero.
The theorem does not determine rank for higher nilpotency layers.
